sentences.text: Challenging judgment and award dated 23.06.2014 passed by Fast Track Court-II and Additional MACT, Belagavi, in MVC no.914/2013, this appeal is filed.

entities.text: Fast Track Court-II and Additional MACT, Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Shri Chandrashekhar M. Hosamani, learned counsel for appellant submitted, appeal was by claimant being aggrieved by dismissal of claim petition filed under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('MV Act' for short).
It was submitted, on 30.12.2012 that claimant was riding Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration no.K-22/Y- 9825 belonging to respondent no.1, insured with respondent no.2.
When rider of an unknown Autorikshaw came from hind side dashed against it and caused accident.
In accident, claimant sustained grievous injuries and despite treatment did not recover fully and sustained loss of earning capacity.
Therefore, claim petition was filed under Section 163-A of MV Act against owner and insurer of Scooter.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3549 HC-KAR 3.
Despite service, owner did not appear and was placed ex parte.
Insurer opposed claim petition on all counts.
4. Based on pleadings, Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.
Claimant along with Dr.Annasaheb B. Patil deposed as PWs.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P14.
Insurer did not lead evidence.

5. while considering, Tribunal relied upon decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Ningamma Sharat Shenappa Shetty vs Karunkar Shetty S/O Bachu Shetty on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4438929/
2 and others V.

sentences.text: United India Insurance Company Limited1 ('Ningamma' for short)

and though assessed compensation towards 'pain and suffering' at Rs.5,000/-, 'loss of income during laid up period' at Rs.13,200/- and 'medical expenses' at Rs.15,000/- i.e., a total of Rs.33,200/-, held it claim petition against under Section 163-A of MV Act against owner and insurer of vehicle by borrower would not be maintainable and dismissed it.

It was submitted, in view of 2009 ACJ 2020 NC:
2026:KHC-D:3549 HC-KAR Three Judges' Bench decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Chandrakant Tiwari Vs. New India Assurance Co. Limited2 ('Chandrakant Tiwari' for short), in a claim petition under Section 163-A of MV Act, claimant would be required to establish that he had sustained injuries on account of use of a motor vehicle and would not be required to establish negligence and claim petition would be maintainable even by borrower of vehicle against owner/insurer, impugned award would not be tenable.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. On other hand, Shri Sharanappa S. Koliwad, learned counsel for respondent no.2-insurer, sought to rely on decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Ramkhiladi and another V. United Insurance Company & another3 ('Ramkhiladi' for short) as well as Ningamma and sought for dismissal.

entities.text: Ramkhiladi and another V. United Insurance Company & another3 ('Ramkhiladi' for
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Alternatively it was submitted, even if insurer is liable, personal accident coverage subscribed to by insured was for maximum of Rs.1,00,000/- 2020 ACJ 2552 (2020) 2 SCC 385 NC:
2026:KHC-D:3549 HC-KAR 7.
Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and award.

8. From above, points that would arise for consideration are:
i.
Whether dismissal of claim petition by Tribunal would be justified?
ii. If not, quantum of compensation, to which claimant would be entitled to?

9 . Point no.1 : Though Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ningamma's case as well as in Ramkhiladi's case had held borrower of a vehicle from owner would step into shoes of owner and therefore cannot maintain claim petition against insurer of said vehicle

, it was in a case of 'liability only act policy',
unlike in present case where there is coverage package policy wherein owner has paid premium for coverage of risk up to Rs.1,00,000/-.

10. In either case, Three Judges Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Chandrakant Tiwari's case has held NC: 2026:KHC-D:3549 HC-KAR claim petition even in case of negligence would be maintainable under Section 163-A of MV Act, award impugned would be maintainable.
Accordingly point no.1 is answered in negative as above.

11. Point no.2 : Insofar as quantum of compensation, since this is a personal injury claim under Section 163-A of MV Act, compensation would require to be paid as per Schedule-II to MV Act,
whereunder Rs.5,000/- is prescribed as compensation towards pain and suffering and maximum of Rs.15,000/- is payable towards 'medical expenses'.
Tribunal has awarded said amount and also awarded Rs.13,200/- towards 'loss of income during laid up period'.
Consequently, claimant would be entitled for amount assessed by Tribunal point no.2 is answered accordingly.

ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3549 HC-KAR ii. Judgment and award dated 23.06.2014 passed by Tribunal in MVC no.914/2013 is set aside.
iii. Claim petition is allowed.

Claimant is entitled for Rs.33,200/- with interest at 6%
per annum from date of claim petition till deposit from owner and insurer with clarification that liability of insurer cannot be beyond sum of Rs.1,00,000/-.
iv.
Insurer is directed to deposit amount towards its liability before Tribunal within six weeks from today.
v. On deposit, Tribunal is directed to release same in favour of claimant forthwith.
vi. Registry is directed to remit the Trial Court Records forthwith.
